sketches.title: Stage Left, Stage Right
sketches.premise: Two stage crews compete to control a runaway play. Each turn, place a real theatre thing that handles the thing currently onstage: a curtain can hide a spotlight, and a spotlight can expose a curtain. The host gives a dry review of every failed bit of stagecraft.
sketches.criterion: A move wins only when the named theatre thing directly blocks, reveals, traps, silences, removes, or otherwise controls what stands; merely moving away, enduring it, or using a larger version of it loses.
sketches.move_shape: Say: "I am [theatre thing], and I [plain action] the [standing thing]." Example: "I am a blackout, and I swallow the spotlight."
sketches.first_card: A spotlight, blazing at center stage.

sketches.title: The Prop Department Has Opinions
sketches.premise: Two prop masters build a chain of stage objects, each one dealing with the prop just handed over. A net can catch a thrown knife, a match can burn a paper crown, and a magnet can claim a metal sword; the host remains unimpressed by anything that is merely a shinier duplicate.
sketches.criterion: The next prop must physically or plainly use, stop, spoil, contain, or transform the standing prop; dodging it, surviving it, or offering a bigger or closely related copy does not count.
sketches.move_shape: Name one ordinary stage prop and its direct action: "I am a bucket, catching the falling paint."
sketches.first_card: A glass bottle, balanced on a stool.

sketches.title: The Last Line
sketches.premise: Actors duel with spoken lines, but every line must directly defeat the dramatic force of the line before it. A question can unsettle a boast, a command can silence a question, and a joke can puncture a threat; the host will not accept a louder version of the same speech.
sketches.criterion: A line overcomes the standing line when its wording directly answers, cancels, exposes, commands, reframes, or makes the earlier line harmless, while ignoring it, merely contradicting it, or shouting harder loses.
sketches.move_shape: Give a short line and explain its effect: "I say, 'Who told you that?' and crack the boast open with doubt."
sketches.first_card: "No one in this room can stop me."

sketches.title: Costume Change
sketches.premise: Two actors race through costume changes, with every new costume having to defeat the role or costume currently worn. A judge's robe can overrule a pirate coat, a raincoat can defeat a paper dress in a storm, and a monster mask can frighten a clown mask; changing into something merely grander is not enough.
sketches.criterion: A costume wins when its role or practical features directly restrain, expose, frighten, command, protect against, or otherwise defeat what is worn, not when it only avoids contact, lasts longer, or belongs to the same costume family.
sketches.move_shape: Say what you wear and what it does: "I wear a police uniform, and its authority stops the pirate's raid."
sketches.first_card: A pirate coat, with a toy sword tucked inside.

sketches.title: Cue to Cue
sketches.premise: The theatre's cues have escaped their script. On each turn, give one clear cue that acts on the cue before it: a curtain cue can hide a set change, a sound cue can drown a speech, and a stop cue can end a dance. The host treats vague timing as a performance of modern confusion.
sketches.criterion: A cue overcomes the standing cue only if it directly triggers, blocks, interrupts, masks, or changes that cue's effect; arriving later, merely matching its strength, or avoiding the moment does not count.
sketches.move_shape: Name a cue and its result: "I give a blackout cue, cutting off the spotlight cue."
sketches.first_card: A spotlight cue: "Lights up on the thief."

sketches.title: Backstage Beasts
sketches.premise: The theatre's puppets and stage creatures wake up and duel in plain sight. Each turn, become a creature that defeats the one before it through an obvious trait: a cat catches a mouse, a bird escapes a cat, and a net catches the bird. The host praises the puppet strings for their restraint.
sketches.criterion: A creature must directly catch, eat, frighten, trap, poison, command, or otherwise overpower the standing creature; fleeing, being too small to notice, lasting longer, or choosing a bigger relative loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name a creature and its action: "I am a frog, and I swallow the fly."
sketches.first_card: A mouse, skittering across the painted stage.
